title: The parol evidence rule: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Gianni v. R. Russel & Co., Inc.: Gianni supplies the restrictive “naturally included” approach. Compare Masterson’s contextual approach to a collateral term and TeeVee Toons’ CISG analysis of the parties’ intent.

Masterson v. Sine: It illustrates partial integration, contextual evidence of completeness, and the difference between excluding a claimed term and deciding whether that term was proved.

Bollinger v. Central Pennsylvania Quarry Stripping and Construction Co.: It explains why the parol evidence rule does not make a mistaken writing immune from correction.

TeeVee Toons, Inc. v. Gerhard Schubert GmbH: TeeVee Toons makes the choice of legal regime concrete: the same dispute about a written agreement receives a different evidentiary analysis under the CISG than under the restrictive domestic approach in Gianni.
